Corrected assignment guidance in PROCESS-CORRECTION.md explicitly applies the aggregate bound to metadata/directory listings as well as policy/source before the first call. Do not claim full process compliance. This process-only incident does not invalidate the independently source-supported public claims or independence.

Opus fetched a pinned tarball, inventoried members before extraction, then extracted beneath its private reviewer directory. This is source acquisition, not execution or test validation; no repository hooks/scripts ran. Effort was coordinator-verified from actual launch arguments; native assistant messages confirm exact model. Sol retained a successful raw transport whose initial strict base64 decode rejected embedded whitespace; corrected decoding verified blob identity. No failed decode contributes behavior evidence. Coordinator initially tried the wrong extracted documentation path, received ENOENT, then located and read the correct pinned file. No mutation or hidden deletion resulted.

## Limits and carry-forward
No runtime experiments or desktop resources created. Preserve all API stdout/stderr/exit receipts and source artifacts. Source reasoning is enough for this scoped advisory review, but does not establish measured GUI or battery behavior. Keep all warning-restoration discussions explicitly limited to pre-existing state. No confirmed review-tool bug or Omadev issue identified.
comment:
No code defect found in the inspected scope. One documentation update is suggested.

**Verified (source inspection):** the popup layout uses the card’s clamped width, and newly issued low-battery warnings receive a finite lifetime without losing their notification-silencing bypass.

| Source-derived behavior | Before | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Card width in the reported 450-logical-pixel, 16px-font example | 507px | 360px |
| New low-battery toast lifetime | No automatic expiry | 12 seconds, paused while hovered |

**Documentation note:** [`docs/notifications.md:168-169`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/703ebfa7adc1357b873790bd0b9031d244ce5f5c/docs/notifications.md#L168-L169) still calls the low-battery toast “critical.” **Suggested change:** describe its normal urgency and 12-second timeout.

**Existing-state limitation:** previously saved critical battery warnings retain their old urgency and still need dismissal; this change prevents persistence of new warnings rather than cleaning up old ones.
